documents.title: think the back thing is back
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Got back from a beach vacation a couple weeks ago and the spots are coming back, on my chest too this time. More obvious since I got some color. I've been scrubbing it in the shower and it's not doing anything. Do I need a new referral to see the dermatologist again or can I just call them?

documents.title: RE: think the back thing is back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Sounds like it may be the same thing. Your insurance wants a referral each year, so I sent a new one this morning. Go ahead and call them to book. Scrubbing won't help it, so you can give your skin a break.

medications.sig: Apply to chest and back as a wash, leave on 5 minutes, rinse. Daily for 2 weeks.

documents.title: Dermatology Follow-up
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group, follow-up visit
Date of visit: 02/28/2024

Mr. Holt is a 24 year old man we first saw last March for tinea versicolor of the back. He comes back with a similar picture. Since a beach vacation, where he spent several days in the sun, he has noticed spots that have spread slowly over the last few weeks. They don't itch, burn or hurt. He thinks they stand out more now that he has a tan. Scrubbing in the shower has not changed them.

ROS: no recent illness, fever, sore throat or weight loss. No joint pain, no night sweats. No new medications.
Medications: none.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family history: noncontributory for skin or atopic disease.
Social: one sexual partner, condoms every time.

Exam: Scattered small oval flat macules over the upper chest and back, lighter than the surrounding skin, with well-defined edges. Most concentrated on the upper back. Gentle fingernail scraping brings up a fine powdery scale. No surrounding redness. Remainder of skin exam normal; hands, feet, groin and face are uninvolved. Palms and soles normal. Oral and conjunctival mucosa clear. No cervical, axillary or inguinal lymphadenopathy.

Assessment: Recurrent tinea versicolor, clinical diagnosis.

Plan:
1. Ketoconazole 2% shampoo to chest and back, 5 minutes then rinse, daily for 2 weeks.
2. Reviewed that the light patches will lag behind the scale and may take months to fill in.
3. Follow up as needed.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in his care.

documents.title: shampoo question
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Quick question. Derm said leave the shampoo on 5 minutes but the pharmacy label just says apply daily. Which is right? Also is it ok to use it on my chest, the label says scalp.

documents.title: RE: shampoo question
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Hi Gavin. Follow the dermatologist's directions: lather it on the chest and back, leave it about 5 minutes, then rinse, once a day for 2 weeks. It's fine to use on the body even though the box is written for the scalp.

documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Pt left voicemail at 6:40 am, car won't start, can't make 8:20 physical. Called back, rescheduled to 10/15 at 8:00. Reminded to come fasting for labs.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
25 yo M for yearly physical (rescheduled from last month).

No meds, NKDA. Never smoker, doesn't vape. Drinks a couple of times a month with friends. One partner, uses condoms. Lifeguarding again this summer.

Exam

HEENT: normal
Neck: no LAD

Abd: soft, NT
Skin: no scale on trunk

results.test: Fungal elements, skin scraping, KOH preparation
results.text: Positive: short curved hyphal filaments and round budding yeast forms

documents.title: Dermatology Office Note
documents.author: dermatology
documents.body:
Outside dermatology group
Visit 03/12/2025

HPI: 25M, followed in our practice for tinea versicolor. He had the same problem after beach travel in 2023 and 2024 and is back after another recent beach trip, with several months of light patches on the upper back and shoulders that do not tan along with the rest of his skin. No itch. Washes often and wears sunscreen and the patches have not budged. No recent illness, no medicines, no international travel.

PSH: wisdom teeth removed at 18.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: no skin or atopic disease in the family.
SH: never smoker, occasional alcohol. Lifeguard in the summer.

Exam: Upper trunk with many small, faintly scaly macules that run together into irregular hypopigmented patches, light scale throughout. No erythema. Nontender.

KOH: short curved filaments and round budding forms seen.

Assessment: Tinea versicolor, recurrent, KOH confirmed. The lightening he notices is mostly the yeast slowing the skin's pigment cells down in those spots, not damage to the skin or loss of the pigment cells, so color returns once the yeast is cleared and the skin gets some sun, typically over a few months.

Plan: ketoconazole 2% shampoo as a body wash, 5 min contact, daily for 14 days. Discussed that this tends to recur with heat and humidity. RTC prn.

documents.title: derm letter
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I saw the derm note in my portal. It says the spots are lighter because of the yeast slowing down my pigment. So is it permanent? This one bugs me more because it's on my shoulders and shows when I'm working.

documents.title: RE: derm letter
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Not permanent. The pigment cells are still there, they just stop working normally under the yeast. Once the shampoo course clears it, the color catches up, usually over a few months, a bit faster once you're in the sun. The yeast part can come back, which is why it has shown up each year.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Physical, 26M.

Tinea versicolor came back again in early March after a beach trip; derm did a KOH (positive) and another 2 week ketoconazole shampoo course. He says the color on his shoulders filled back in over the late spring. Nothing on the skin now.

Meds none. NKDA. Never smoker. Alcohol occasional. Still lifeguarding summers.

Exam: vitals ok. Pleasant, well. HEENT wnl. Neck supple, no nodes or thyromegaly. Heart regular, no murmur. Lungs clear to bases. Abd soft. Skin: trunk without scale. No edema.

PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 2.

A/P
- Tinea versicolor, recurrent, yearly in the spring and summer, managed by derm with topical courses. He asked about a way to keep it from coming back; told him to bring it up at his next derm visit, some people do a monthly wash in the warm months.
- Flu shot today. Declines covid vaccine this season.
- Labs: CBC, CMP, lipids, TSH.
- Tdap next due 2032.
- RTC 1 year.

documents.title: Your labs
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Everything from your physical is normal, including thyroid and cholesterol. Enjoy the fall.
